questions.q: Who personally carved 'Korean Territory' into the rock on Dokdo's Dongdo (East Islet)?
questions.fact: In August 1953, [[Hong Sun-chil]] carved 'Korean Territory' into a rock on Dongdo (East Islet).
questions.explain: The source dates the carving to August 5, 1953. The three characters remain on the rock.
questions.deep: Hong Sun-chil came from Ulleungdo. In 1953, amid the aftermath of the Korean War, he organized 33 volunteers to defend Dokdo when the state's capacity to protect it was limited. On August 5, 1953, he carved 'Korean Territory' into a rock on Dongdo (East Islet). Rather than leaving a removable sign, he cut the declaration directly into stone. The volunteers later handed their duties to the police in 1956. Hong also raised money for weapons by trading squid. These were practical efforts by civilians to protect the island. Dokdo's road names honor Isabu and An Yong-bok. Hong's name is not a road name, but his inscription remains part of the island itself.

wrong.0: Isabu conquered Usan State in 512, roughly 1,400 years earlier.
wrong.1: An Yong-bok was active in the seventeenth century.
wrong.3: Choi began living on Dokdo in 1965, after the inscription was made.

questions.q: In which year did Japan's Dajokan issue its directive stating that Ulleungdo and Dokdo had nothing to do with Japan?
questions.fact: Japan's Dajokan issued the directive on Ulleungdo and Dokdo in [[1877]].
questions.explain: The Dajokan was Japan's highest decision-making authority. Its directive stated that Ulleungdo and Dokdo had nothing to do with Japan.
questions.deep: The Dajokan was the highest governing body of early Meiji Japan, comparable to the later cabinet. In March 1877 it directed that Ulleungdo and the other island had nothing to do with Japan. The attached map helps identify the other island as Dokdo. The inquiry arose during a land-registry survey. Shimane Prefecture asked the Home Ministry whether the islands should be included. The ministry investigated historical records and referred the question to the Dajokan. The directive came after that investigation, not from a private opinion. It is a record produced by Japan's own central government. In 1905, just 28 years later, Japan claimed to incorporate Dokdo as ownerless territory. The source contrasts that claim with the earlier directive and notes its absence from Japanese promotional accounts.

wrong.0: 1868 is the year of the Meiji Restoration, nine years earlier.
wrong.2: 1895 is associated with the end of the First Sino-Japanese War.
wrong.3: 1905 is the year Japan claimed to incorporate Dokdo.

questions.q: Who was Dokdo's first civilian resident?
questions.fact: Dokdo's first civilian resident, who settled there in 1965, was [[Choi Jong-deok]].
questions.explain: Choi Jong-deok settled on Seodo (West Islet) in 1965 and made a living gathering seafood.
questions.deep: Choi Jong-deok was a diver from Ulleungdo. In March 1965 he settled on Seodo (West Islet), gathering abalone, turban snails and sea cucumbers. He built 998 cement steps to reach the Mulgol water source. This was difficult physical work necessary for daily life, not simply a symbolic visit. His presence differed from that of the guards: he was a civilian earning a living on the island. Kim Sung-do and his wife later continued civilian residence there. The supplied source states that Kim Shin-yeol died in March 2026, leaving no permanent civilian residents, and contrasts this with 112 Japanese registrations of permanent domicile. These time-specific statements are retained as source claims and require editorial verification before publication.

wrong.0: Kim Sung-do continued civilian residence after Choi.
wrong.2: Hong led the volunteer garrison; the question asks about civilian settlement.
wrong.3: An was a seventeenth-century fisherman, not the modern resident described here.

questions.q: Which old name for Dokdo came from the many sea lions living there?
questions.fact: Dokdo's old name [[Gajido]] came from gaji-eo, an old term for sea lions.
questions.explain: Sea lions were once called gaji-eo. Their abundance gave the island the name Gajido.
questions.deep: The Annals of King Jeongjo record a governor's report referring to Gajido and four or five sea lions. The name preserves a link between the island and the animals living there. The names Keungajebawi and Jageungajebawi, the large and small gaje rocks, preserve the same association. Place names can carry traces of earlier ecology. Usando, Seokdo and Gajido belong to different historical contexts. They should not be treated as interchangeable labels without considering their sources and dates. The source states that the sea lion was classified as extinct by the IUCN in 1994. The animal disappeared, but its old name remains in Dokdo's place names.

wrong.0: Usando is a name found in official historical records, not one derived from sea lions.
wrong.1: Sambongdo refers to three peaks.
wrong.3: Seokdo means stone island.

questions.q: In which year did Shimane Prefecture establish the observance it calls 'Takeshima Day' for its claim to Dokdo?
questions.fact: Shimane Prefecture established its so-called 'Takeshima Day' in [[2005]].
questions.explain: The prefecture chose February 22, marking the centenary of its 1905 incorporation notice.
questions.deep:
The date February 22 refers to Shimane Notice No. 40 of 1905. A century later, in 2005, Shimane Prefecture established the observance through a local ordinance.

Although it began as a prefectural event, senior officials from Japan's central government have attended. The source interprets this as giving national support to the territorial claim.

It also connects the event with repeated proposals for an ICJ referral: both are presented as ways to make Dokdo appear internationally disputed.

Korea's Dokdo Day is October 25, recalling Imperial Edict No. 41 of 1900. The source emphasizes the contrast with the Japanese notice issued five years later.

wrong.0: 1995 was ten years before the ordinance.
wrong.1: 2000 was five years before the ordinance.
wrong.3: 2010 was five years after the ordinance.

questions.q: In which year was the Dokdo Volunteer Garrison formed?
questions.fact: Hong Sun-chil and 33 young volunteers formed the Dokdo Volunteer Garrison in [[1953]].
questions.explain: The garrison was formed in 1953, during the Korean War period, to defend Dokdo.
questions.deep:
In the confusion surrounding the Korean War and armistice, Japanese patrol vessels approached Dokdo and territorial markers appeared. Hong Sun-chil and fellow islanders organized a civilian defense force.

Hong used money from his grandfather and profits from squid trading to buy equipment in Busan and Daegu, including M1 rifles and a mortar. Their resources did not simply arrive as government aid.

They also painted logs black to resemble large guns. The source says a Japanese magazine reported these as artillery and that aircraft approaches decreased. This is the story behind the garrison's well-known deception.

In 1956, the volunteers handed their duties to the national police. Civilian defense was followed by regular state policing.

wrong.0: 1948 predates the garrison's formation.
wrong.1: 1950 is the year the Korean War began.
wrong.3: 1956 is the handover year, not the formation year.

questions.q: How many times did An Yong-bok travel to Japan to assert that Dokdo belonged to Joseon?
questions.fact: An Yong-bok traveled to Japan [[twice]], in 1693 and 1696.
questions.explain: His first journey in 1693 followed his abduction; his second, in 1696, was voluntary.
questions.deep:
The two journeys had different beginnings. In 1693, Japanese fishermen abducted An Yong-bok from Ulleungdo. Even as a captive, he asserted Joseon's ownership before officials in Hoki.

In 1696 he went voluntarily, carrying information about Joseon's territory. The Murakami family of the Oki Islands kept records of this visit.

The supplied account connects his actions with the shogunate's ban on travel to Ulleungdo. The precise sequence of the January 1696 ban and his later second journey requires care: they must not be placed in reverse order.

After returning, he was punished with exile for traveling abroad without authorization. His territorial advocacy and his treatment by the Joseon court are distinct parts of the story.

wrong.0: This counts only one of the two journeys.
wrong.2: The records discussed here concern two journeys.
wrong.3: Four doubles the number of journeys.

Below the surface the two islets form parts of the same volcanic body. The surrounding seabed lies roughly 2,000 m down, and the source gives the volcanic structure a total height of about 2,270 m.

What appears to be a small area of land is only the summit of a much larger underwater feature.

The 1905 notice therefore brought together commercial interests and Japan's military strategy during the Russo-Japanese War. It was not merely the discovery of an unknown island.

questions.q: In which year did the Edo shogunate officially ban Japanese people from traveling to Ulleungdo?

questions.deep: The 1696 ban did not arise by chance. The shogunate investigated the matter following the dispute in which An Yong-bok had asserted Joseon's position. It first asked Tottori Domain about Ulleungdo's jurisdiction. The domain officially replied that neither Ulleungdo nor Dokdo belonged to it. A Japanese local authority thus stated that the islands were outside its jurisdiction. After receiving the reply, the shogunate prohibited Japanese travel to Ulleungdo. The decision followed an investigation; it was not merely an improvised diplomatic concession. The ban continued to be enforced. In 1837, 141 years later, Hachiemon was executed after violating it and traveling to Ulleungdo. This was more than a rule left on paper. The exact chronology of the ban and An's second journey is noted separately in the editorial review.

choices: Dokdo was uninhabited and therefore excluded from talks
The treaty uses examples, while SCAPIN 677 supports exclusion from Japan
Japan voluntarily promised to return Dokdo
Korean occupation made a written reference unnecessary
questions.fact: The source cites [[SCAPIN 677]] as a key document supporting Korea's position despite Dokdo's omission from the treaty.
questions.distractor: Article 3 of the San Francisco Treaty
blankDistractors: Article 3 of the San Francisco Treaty
questions.explain: Article 2 provides for Japan to renounce rights to Korea, including Jeju-do, Geomundo and Ulleungdo. The source reads 'including' as illustrative rather than an exhaustive list.
questions.deep: This question was unusual in the original poll: 48% chose the claim that Korean occupation made a written reference unnecessary. The source considers this a weak legal explanation; occupation alone cannot automatically establish title. Its first argument concerns the treaty's illustrative wording. The phrase 'including Jeju-do, Geomundo and Ulleungdo' is read as examples of Korean islands, not as limiting the renunciation to those three. Its second argument concerns SCAPIN 677 of 1946, which expressly excluded Dokdo from Japanese political and administrative jurisdiction. Omission from a later list and explicit earlier administrative exclusion are different kinds of evidence. The source links the treaty's drafting history to Japanese diplomacy and the Rusk letter. It emphasizes that a view expressed by the United States was not itself an agreement by all treaty parties. These are the source's arguments, not a claim that SCAPIN alone was a final sovereignty judgment.

wrong.2: The source records no voluntary Japanese promise of this kind.
wrong.3: This was the most common wrong answer. Occupation alone is not the legal explanation presented.

questions.deep: SCAP instructions were directives issued by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers to Japan's government. Two are particularly relevant to Dokdo. No. 677, dated January 29, 1946, excluded Dokdo from Japanese political and administrative jurisdiction, alongside Ulleungdo and Jeju-do. The source treats this as important evidence of the Allied administrative treatment of the islands after the war. No. 1033, issued in June 1946, prohibited Japanese vessels and crews from approaching within twelve nautical miles of Dokdo. The first concerned administration; the second restricted physical approach. Remembering the two together helps distinguish their functions. The source invokes them in response to arguments based on Dokdo not being named in the final San Francisco Peace Treaty. Both belong to the history of the US-led Allied occupation. Their precise scope must be read in the documents rather than assumed to be a final determination of sovereignty.

An official place name appears in maps, nautical charts and public records. It can also enter internationally used geographical databases. Naming is therefore more than a symbolic gesture. The original text additionally makes a 2026 claim about the IHO's S-130 digital standard and the use of identifiers. This time-sensitive technical claim has not been independently verified for this translation and is flagged for review. Its broader point is that names also matter within digital data structures.

questions.q: What factor does the supplied account emphasize in the ICJ's 2008 Pedra Branca judgment in Singapore's favor?
questions.fact: The supplied account emphasizes [[long-term effective administration]] in the Pedra Branca judgment.
questions.explain: It describes lighthouse operations and administrative activity as important evidence, while noting that historical origin alone was not decisive.
questions.deep: Pedra Branca is a small maritime feature between Malaysia and Singapore. The source contrasts Malaysia's historical-title argument with Singapore's record of administration. The Court found for Singapore over Pedra Branca. The supplied account dates lighthouse-related activity to 1847 and highlights construction and administrative acts. The precise chronology and legal reasoning require consultation of the judgment, not this summary alone. The source compares those activities with Korea's police, lighthouse and administrative presence on Dokdo since 1954. This is an educational analogy, not an ICJ determination about Dokdo. The same judgment awarded nearby Middle Rocks to Malaysia. Evidence was assessed for each feature separately. Korea also maintains that Dokdo is not a territorial dispute to be submitted to the Court. The analogy therefore has limits.

wrong.1: The question does not describe a transfer by treaty.

questions.q: Which potential future energy resource is thought to lie beneath the seabed near Dokdo?
questions.fact: The potential energy resource thought to lie beneath the seabed near Dokdo is [[methane hydrate]].
questions.explain: The supplied source estimates about 600 million tonnes of methane hydrate, often called 'burning ice.' This is an estimate, not a proven commercially recoverable reserve.
questions.deep: Methane hydrate forms when methane is trapped within water molecules under low-temperature, high-pressure conditions. Its ice-like appearance and ability to burn give it the nickname burning ice. Deep parts of the East Sea provide those conditions. The source cites an average surrounding seabed depth of about 2,000 m and an estimated quantity of 600 million tonnes. The word estimated matters. A deposit and an economically recoverable reserve are not the same. The text notes that commercial production methods are not yet established and that methane leakage could worsen greenhouse warming. The resource illustrates why discussion of Dokdo extends beyond its 187,554 m² of exposed land to surrounding waters. The source also cites an estimated annual combined marine-resource value of about KRW 11 trillion; that estimate is not verified revenue.

wrong.0: Oil is not the potential resource asked for in this item.
wrong.2: Phosphate is a mineral resource, not the fuel described.
wrong.3: This option refers to ordinary gaseous fuel rather than the solid hydrate structure.

Adding resources without established commercial extraction technology can greatly increase the figure. This is an estimate of potential value, not a stream of realized earnings. The source uses the estimate to show that interests surrounding Dokdo concern maritime resources as well as the symbolism of a small rocky island. Claims about maritime zones still require their own legal analysis.

questions.q: Which of these Korean islands has the oldest volcanic origin?
questions.fact: Among these Korean volcanic islands, [[Dokdo]] formed earliest, about 4.6 million years ago.
questions.explain: The source gives approximate formation ages of 4.6 million years for Dokdo, 2.5 million for Ulleungdo and 1.8 million for Jeju-do.
questions.deep: The order can be surprising: the largest of the three, Jeju-do, is the youngest in the supplied comparison, while the smallest, Dokdo, is the oldest. Erosion helps explain the contrast. Waves have worn Dokdo down over millions of years. Its sea cliffs, sea stacks and weathering cavities record the long reshaping of the original volcanic body. Below the surface, the scale is much larger. The source gives a surrounding seabed depth of about 2,000 m and a volcanic height of about 2,270 m. The visible rocks are only the summit. Geological age does not itself establish sovereignty. It does, however, contribute to the geological value of Dokdo's protected natural environment.

wrong.0: The source dates Jeju-do to about 1.8 million years ago.
wrong.1: Ulleungdo is dated to about 2.5 million years ago, later than Dokdo.
wrong.3: Geojedo is described here as an island separated from the mainland, not one of these volcanic islands.

questions.deep: The point is not only who is there, but why the source emphasizes police. It interprets this as reflecting Korea's treatment of Dokdo as normally administered domestic territory, not a military confrontation zone. This is not a universal rule deciding sovereignty. The three groups perform different functions: police maintain public order, lighthouse keepers operate navigation aids, and county staff administer the island. Together they represent an operating public-service system. The supplied account gives the police rotation as about two months and describes round-the-clock work under difficult conditions. It dates the permanent police presence to 1954. It additionally states that Kim Shin-yeol died in March 2026, leaving no permanent civilian residents while official personnel remained. That time-sensitive statement is flagged for editorial verification.

choices: Geography of the Annals of King Sejong
questions.fact: The 1454 [[Geography of the Annals of King Sejong]] records that Usan and Mureung can be seen from one another in clear weather.

questions.deep: The record says that Usan and Mureung are two islands, not far apart, and visible in clear weather. That short statement contains several kinds of information. First, it treats them as two distinct islands, rather than one island with two names. The source contrasts this with arguments that Usando was merely another name for Ulleungdo or an imaginary island. Second, it records visibility. Dokdo can be seen from high ground on Ulleungdo on clear days, across the distance now measured as 87.4 km. Third, the text is an officially compiled geography, not a private travel diary. The source compares its date with the Japanese geography book Onshu Shicho Goki of 1667, 213 years later.

questions.q: Which president rewrote a draft overnight before delivering the 2006 special address on Korea-Japan relations?
questions.fact: The president who personally rewrote the 2006 special address overnight was [[Roh Moo-hyun]].
questions.explain: Roh Moo-hyun delivered the address in April 2006 in response to Japan's attempted hydrographic survey near Dokdo.
questions.deep: In April 2006, two Japanese survey vessels set out toward Dokdo. The government had to decide its response, and advisers prepared a restrained diplomatic draft. The president set that draft aside and worked on the wording overnight. The speech described Dokdo not simply as Korean land, but as land bearing the painful history of Japanese imperial aggression. The source sees this as a change in framing: from a negotiable territorial issue to a question of addressing the historical legacy of colonial aggression. It cites a 94.6% favorable public response and describes the speech as unusually explicit in its position toward Japan. Those polling and comparative claims belong to the supplied source and have not been remeasured for this edition.

questions.q: Which bird is most commonly seen on Dokdo?
questions.fact: Dokdo's most familiar bird, known for its cat-like cry, is the [[black-tailed gull]].
questions.explain: Thousands of black-tailed gulls visit Dokdo to breed each spring. Their Korean name refers to a cry resembling a cat's.
questions.deep: The Korean word gwaengi is an old word for a cat. The black-tailed gull's call explains its Korean name, gwaengi-galmaegi, and is a familiar sound in live broadcasts from Dokdo. Thousands arrive in spring to lay eggs and raise chicks. Restricted human access and abundant food in the surrounding waters help make the island suitable for breeding. A breeding ground is not the same as a temporary rest stop. It supports successive generations. The source links this ecological importance to Dokdo's natural-monument protection in 1982. Dokdo also serves as a stopover for birds crossing the East Sea. Between Ulleungdo and the more distant Oki Islands, a small patch of land can provide a valuable place to rest.

wrong.0: The eagle is not Dokdo's most common bird.
wrong.2: Streaked shearwaters are observed, but are not the most common bird here.
wrong.3: Kestrels are birds of prey and are much less numerous.

questions.src: 유엔 해양법 담당 부서 · United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, Part VI, Article 77(1)-(3): https://static.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part6.htm
questions.q: How does UNCLOS describe a coastal state's continental-shelf rights in relation to occupation and proclamation?
choices: rights created only by a formal proclamation
rights created only by resource extraction
rights created only by actual occupation
rights independent of occupation or proclamation
questions.fact: The coastal state holds [[rights independent of occupation or proclamation]] over its continental shelf under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: rights created only by actual occupation
blankDistractors: rights created only by a formal proclamation
rights created only by resource extraction
rights created only by actual occupation
questions.explain: Article 77(3) does not make these rights depend on occupation or a proclamation. This concerns continental-shelf rights, not a method of acquiring sovereignty over an island.

wrong.0: The article expressly makes the rights independent of a proclamation.
wrong.1: Leaving resources undeveloped does not remove the coastal state's rights or allow anyone to exploit them.
wrong.2: Actual occupation is not a prerequisite for these continental-shelf rights.

questions.src: 국제사법재판소 · Statute of the International Court of Justice, Article 41: https://icj-web.leman.un-icc.cloud/statute
questions.q: What is the purpose of provisional measures at the International Court of Justice before a final decision?
choices: changing the terms of a treaty
questions.fact: Under Article 41 of the ICJ Statute, [[preserving the parties' rights]] is the purpose of provisional measures.
blankDistractors: changing the terms of a treaty
questions.explain: Provisional measures protect the parties' rights while the case remains undecided. Their indication does not itself settle who wins the case on its merits.

wrong.2: Provisional measures do not automatically create the Court's authority to decide a dispute.
wrong.3: Interim protection of rights is different from a final decision on the merits.

questions.fact: Absent an international-standard exception, the safety zone normally extends at most [[500 m]] from the artificial island's outer edge.
questions.explain: Article 60(5) measures this distance from the outer edge. Internationally authorized exceptions and the actual zone width are separate matters.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part7.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS, where does a pursued ship's entry end a lawfully begun right of hot pursuit?
choices: the first stretch of high seas
the pursuing state's exclusive economic zone
the territorial sea of its flag state or a third state
questions.fact: The right of hot pursuit ends when the pursued ship enters [[the territorial sea of its flag state or a third state]] under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: the pursuing state's exclusive economic zone
blankDistractors: the first stretch of high seas
the pursuing state's exclusive economic zone
questions.explain: Article 111(3) sets this stopping point. Simply reaching the high seas does not necessarily end a lawful pursuit.

wrong.0: This is not the stopping point specified in the article.
wrong.1: A lawful pursuit can continue onto the high seas when its conditions are met.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part7.htm
questions.q: In UNCLOS, what does a ship's flag state mean?
choices: the state granting the ship the right to fly its flag
the state that bought the cargo
the state where the captain was born
the state with the nearest port
questions.fact: [[The state granting the ship the right to fly its flag]] is its flag state under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: The state where the captain was born
blankDistractors: the state that bought the cargo
the state where the captain was born
the state with the nearest port
questions.explain: Article 91 links a ship's nationality to its entitlement to fly a state's flag. The captain's birthplace or destination does not determine that nationality.

wrong.2: A ship and its captain need not have the same nationality.
wrong.3: Distance to a port does not determine a ship's nationality.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XVI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part16.htm
questions.q: What duty does UNCLOS Article 303 impose on states regarding archaeological and historical objects found at sea?
choices: a duty to assess only their present utility
a duty to grant unconditional ownership to the finder
a duty to protect them and cooperate
a duty to auction them immediately
questions.fact: [[A duty to protect them and cooperate]] applies to states under Article 303 for archaeological and historical objects found at sea.
questions.distractor: A duty to auction them immediately
blankDistractors: a duty to assess only their present utility
a duty to grant unconditional ownership to the finder
a duty to auction them immediately
questions.explain: The article emphasizes protection and cooperation. Finding an object does not automatically grant unrestricted disposal rights.

wrong.1: The article does not grant unconditional ownership to finders.
wrong.3: This replaces protection with an unsupported requirement to sell.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XII · https://static.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part12.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 198, what should a state do upon learning of an imminent pollution threat to other states?
choices: notify only after cleanup is complete
privately notify only its own ships
immediate notice to affected states and competent organizations
questions.fact: Article 198 requires [[immediate notice to affected states and competent organizations]] when such a pollution threat becomes known.
questions.distractor: notice only after cleanup is complete
blankDistractors: notify only after cleanup is complete
privately notify only its own ships
questions.explain: The duty concerns timely warning when the threat becomes known. Cleanup or compensation need not finish before notification.

wrong.0: This improperly delays immediate notification.
wrong.1: This omits affected states and competent organizations.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part6.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 79, whose consent is needed to delineate a pipeline route on the continental shelf?
questions.fact: Delineating a pipeline route on a coastal state's continental shelf requires consent from [[the coastal state]] under UNCLOS.
questions.explain: Article 79(3) addresses the route of pipelines. Its wording should not be treated as an identical rule for every submarine cable.

wrong.1: This does not require unanimous approval by all UN members.
wrong.3: The manufacturing location does not determine this consent right.

questions.src: UN Treaty Series · UNCLOS, authentic texts and conclusion date · https://www.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/unclos_f.pdf
questions.q: Roughly when was UNCLOS drawn up?
questions.fact: UNCLOS was concluded in [[1982]] at Montego Bay.
questions.explain: It was concluded on December 10, 1982. Conclusion, global entry into force and entry into force for a particular state are different dates.

questions.src: UN Treaty Series · UNCLOS, authentic texts and conclusion date · https://www.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/unclos_f.pdf
questions.q: In which year was UNCLOS concluded at Montego Bay?
questions.fact: UNCLOS was concluded in [[1982]] at Montego Bay.
questions.explain: It was concluded on December 10, 1982. Conclusion, global entry into force and entry into force for a particular state are different dates.

wrong.3: This is twenty years before conclusion.

questions.src: UN Treaty Series · UNCLOS, authentic texts and conclusion date · https://www.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/unclos_f.pdf
questions.q: Give the exact year the convention was signed at Montego Bay.
questions.fact: UNCLOS was concluded in [[1982]] at Montego Bay.
questions.explain: It was concluded on December 10, 1982. Conclusion, global entry into force and entry into force for a particular state are different dates.

wrong.2: This is one year after conclusion.

questions.src: ITLOS · M/V Saiga, dissenting opinion reproducing UNCLOS Article 73 in paragraph 4 · https://itlos.org/fileadmin/itlos/documents/cases/1/C1-J-4_Dec_97-DO_PNCVN.pdf
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 73, what condition is linked to prompt release after an EEZ fisheries arrest?
choices: donation of all catches to an international body
permanent immigration applications by the crew
a change to the coastal state's nationality
provision of a reasonable bond or other security
questions.fact: Article 73 links prompt release of arrested vessels and crews to [[provision of a reasonable bond or other security]] under its fisheries rules.
questions.distractor: a change to the coastal state's nationality
blankDistractors: donation of all catches to an international body
permanent immigration applications by the crew
a change to the coastal state's nationality
questions.explain: Article 73(2) requires prompt release upon a reasonable bond or other security. Release does not itself erase the alleged violation.

wrong.1: The rule concerns bond or other security, not immigration.
wrong.2: The article does not make a change of nationality the release condition.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XIII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part13.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 261, what must research equipment avoid causing on established international shipping routes?
questions.fact: Article 261 prohibits [[an obstruction to navigation]] arising from research equipment on established international shipping routes.
questions.explain: A scientific purpose does not authorize blocking shipping routes. Article 261 addresses navigation when research equipment is deployed or used.

wrong.2: The provision does not prohibit disclosing equipment locations.
wrong.3: The article targets obstruction of navigation, not temperature measurement itself.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part6.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 81, who has the exclusive right to authorize and regulate drilling on a continental shelf?
choices: the first institution to map the seabed
the first state to send a drilling vessel
the company selling the drilling equipment
questions.fact: Under Article 81, [[the coastal state]] has the exclusive right to authorize and regulate drilling on the continental shelf for all purposes.
questions.distractor: The first state to send a drilling vessel
blankDistractors: the first institution to map the seabed
the first state to send a drilling vessel
the company selling the drilling equipment
questions.explain: Article 81 covers coastal-state authorization and regulation of drilling for all purposes. Arriving first with a vessel does not replace that right.

wrong.2: The rule does not allocate drilling authority on a first-arrival basis.
wrong.3: Selling equipment does not confer the legal authority.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XIII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part13.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 241, what cannot be based on marine scientific research activities themselves?
choices: observations used to explain marine processes
a legal basis for claims to the marine environment or resources
information used to design further studies
questions.fact: Marine scientific research activities cannot themselves form [[a legal basis for claims to the marine environment or resources]] under Article 241.
blankDistractors: observations used to explain marine processes
information used to design further studies
questions.explain: Scientific research and acquisition of legal rights are different matters. A research vessel's first visit does not itself confer those rights.

wrong.0: Producing scientific observations is different from creating a legal basis for claims.
wrong.1: The article does not prohibit scientific use of temperature records.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part7.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 92, how may a ship using multiple national flags according to convenience be treated?
choices: as automatically registered to the UN
as immune from responsibility in all waters
questions.fact: A ship using multiple flags according to convenience may be treated [[as a ship without nationality]] under Article 92.
blankDistractors: as automatically registered to the UN
as immune from responsibility in all waters
questions.explain: Article 92(2) denies such a ship the ability to claim those nationalities against another state and permits treatment as stateless. This differs from a genuine lawful change of registry.

wrong.0: This does not automatically turn the vessel into a UN ship.
wrong.2: The article does not guarantee simultaneous nationalities.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 독도의 자연환경 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=67
questions.q: Roughly when did Dokdo's weather gear change to ASOS?
questions.fact: Dokdo's AWS was replaced by an ASOS in [[2009]], in December.
questions.explain: The official account dates the ASOS replacement to December 2009. Distinguish the initial automation from a later equipment replacement.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 독도의 자연환경 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=67
questions.q: In which year was Dokdo's AWS replaced by an automated synoptic observing system (ASOS)?
questions.fact: Dokdo's AWS was replaced by an ASOS in [[2009]], in December.
questions.explain: The official account dates the ASOS replacement to December 2009. Distinguish the initial automation from a later equipment replacement.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 독도의 자연환경 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=67
questions.q: Give the exact year the AWS was replaced by ASOS.
questions.fact: Dokdo's AWS was replaced by an ASOS in [[2009]], in December.
questions.explain: The official account dates the ASOS replacement to December 2009. Distinguish the initial automation from a later equipment replacement.

wrong.0: This is one year before the recorded replacement.
wrong.1: This is one year after the ASOS replacement.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XVI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part16.htm
questions.q: What does UNCLOS Article 300 require when states fulfil obligations and exercise rights?
choices: exemption from all duties on national-interest grounds
unlimited rights for the first state to act
good-faith fulfilment and avoidance of abuse of rights
questions.fact: Article 300 requires [[good-faith fulfilment and avoidance of abuse of rights]] under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: unlimited rights for the first state to act
blankDistractors: exemption from all duties on national-interest grounds
unlimited rights for the first state to act
questions.explain: Possessing a right does not mean it may be exercised in any manner. The Convention requires good faith and rules out abuse of rights.

wrong.0: The principle regulates the exercise of rights rather than abolishing them.
wrong.1: The article does not waive every obligation on national-interest grounds.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part6.htm
questions.q: What defines sedentary species included in continental-shelf resources under UNCLOS Article 77?
choices: free surface swimming without seabed contact
flying above the sea throughout life
immobility or movement requiring constant seabed contact
migration into land rivers for every breeding season
questions.fact: Article 77 defines sedentary species by [[immobility or movement requiring constant seabed contact]] at the harvestable stage.
questions.distractor: free surface swimming without seabed contact
blankDistractors: free surface swimming without seabed contact
flying above the sea throughout life
migration into land rivers for every breeding season
questions.explain: The definition concerns organisms immobile on or under the seabed, or unable to move without constant contact at the harvestable stage. It does not include every fish above the shelf.

wrong.0: This does not match the constant-contact criterion for sedentary species.
wrong.3: The test concerns mobility and seabed contact at the harvestable stage, not breeding migration.

questions.src: 해양수산부 포항지방해양수산청 · 독도항로표지관리소 · 등대기능의 등질 항목: https://pohang.mof.go.kr/ko/page.do?menuIdx=2931
questions.q: How many seconds apart are the white flashes of Dokdo Lighthouse?
questions.fact: At Dokdo Lighthouse, [[10 seconds]] separate successive white flashes.
questions.explain: The official light characteristic is one white flash every 10 seconds. Flash timing and the distance the light reaches are different measurements.

wrong.1: This would make the flashes ten times as frequent as specified.

questions.src: 환경부 · 대한민국 정책브리핑 · 울릉도·독도·제주도 첫 국가지질공원 인증(2012-12-27): https://m.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148754196
questions.q: Which natural-heritage program first certified Ulleungdo and Dokdo in 2012?
questions.fact: Ulleungdo and Dokdo received [[National Geopark]] certification in 2012.
questions.explain: Ulleungdo and Dokdo became a National Geopark in 2012. The program combines geological conservation with education and tourism.

wrong.0: National Park designation is different from National Geopark certification.
wrong.2: The question concerns a national geopark certification, not World Heritage inscription.

questions.src: 국사편찬위원회 · 세종실록 153권 지리지, 강원도 삼척도호부 울진현: https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kda_40009004_002 | 외교부 독도 · 세종실록 지리지 역문: https://dokdo.mofa.go.kr/kor/pds/part06_view02.jsp
questions.q: Which local entry in the geography section of the Annals of King Sejong describes Usan and Mureung?
questions.fact: The [[Uljin]] entry in the geography section of the Annals of King Sejong describes Usan and Mureung.
questions.explain: The passage appears in the Uljin entry. Read the historical entry itself rather than assuming that modern administrative boundaries apply.

questions.src: 국사편찬위원회 · 사료로 본 한국사, 신라의 우산국 정복 · 삼국사기 권4 지증마립간 13년: https://contents.history.go.kr/front/hm/view.do?levelId=hm_011_0030 | 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 법흥왕: https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0022785
questions.q: Which Silla king was reigning when the Samguk Sagi records Usan State's surrender?
questions.fact: The Samguk Sagi places Usan State's surrender in the reign of [[King Jijeung]] of Silla.
questions.explain: The Samguk Sagi dates the event to 512, the thirteenth year of King Jijeung's reign. Distinguish the reigning king from Isabu, who led the expedition.

questions.src: 유엔 해양법 담당 부서 · United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, Part XIII, Article 246(2)-(3): https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part13.htm
questions.q: Whose consent is generally required for marine scientific research in another country's exclusive economic zone (EEZ)?
questions.fact: Marine scientific research in an EEZ generally requires consent from [[the coastal state]] under UNCLOS.
questions.explain: Article 246 sets coastal-state consent as the general rule. In normal circumstances, consent for qualifying peaceful research must not be unreasonably delayed or denied.

wrong.1: The vessel's registration does not replace the coastal state's consent.
wrong.3: This article calls for coastal-state consent, not blanket permission from an international organization.

questions.src: 국립국어원 · 지역어 종합 정보, 사진으로 보는 생활어 '떼배' · 2012년 민족생활어 조사 2, 울릉군 도동리: https://dialect.korean.go.kr/dialect/pub/region_culture_sub?regionPhotoId=2691 | 지역별 재료 차이 참고: 한국민족문화대백과사전 '떼배': https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0017208
questions.q: Which plant is named as the material for ttebae rafts in the National Institute of Korean Language's 2012 Ulleungdo survey?
questions.fact: The 2012 Ulleungdo survey records [[paulownia]] as the material used for ttebae rafts.
questions.explain: The Dodong-ri survey describes small working rafts made from paulownia logs. This does not mean that rafts in every region used the same material.

wrong.0: Do not confuse materials used elsewhere with this survey, which names paulownia.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 독도박물관: https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0015954 | 국회도서관 · 독도 연표 1966-2000년, 1997년 8월 8일 항목: https://dokdo.nanet.go.kr/dokdo/front.dokdo?menu=chronology_8
questions.q: In which year did Dokdo Museum first open?
questions.fact: Dokdo Museum opened in [[1997]] on Ulleungdo.
questions.explain: Dokdo Museum opened on August 8, 1997. The start of the museum project should not be confused with its public opening.

questions.src: 외교부 독도 · 무변불유, 대한매일신보(1906-05-01): https://dokdo.mofa.go.kr/kor/pds/part02_view06.jsp | 관련 신문 대조: 대한제국의 독도 관할 자료 목록: https://dokdo.mofa.go.kr/kor/pds/part_list02.jsp
questions.q: Which newspaper published the Dokdo-related article 'Mubyeonbulyu' on May 1, 1906?
questions.fact: [[Daehan Maeil Shinbo]] published the Dokdo-related article 'Mubyeonbulyu' on May 1, 1906.
questions.explain: The article in Daehan Maeil Shinbo reported Sim Heung-taek's account and the Interior Ministry's response. Compare the article title and date, not just the general topic.

wrong.0: Its related article in the foreign ministry's collection is dated May 9, 1906, not the article asked about.
wrong.1: It also carried a related report on May 1, 1906, but that was a different article.

questions.src: 유엔 해양법 담당 부서 · United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, Part VI, Article 77(1)-(3): https://static.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part6.htm
questions.q: How does UNCLOS describe a coastal state's continental-shelf rights in relation to occupation and proclamation?
choices: rights independent of occupation or proclamation
rights created only by actual occupation
rights created only by a formal proclamation
rights created only by resource extraction
questions.fact: The coastal state holds [[rights independent of occupation or proclamation]] over its continental shelf under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: rights created only by actual occupation
questions.explain: Article 77(3) does not make these rights depend on occupation or a proclamation. This concerns continental-shelf rights, not a method of acquiring sovereignty over an island.
blankDistractors: rights created only by actual occupation
rights created only by a formal proclamation
rights created only by resource extraction

wrong.1: Actual occupation is not a prerequisite for these continental-shelf rights.
wrong.2: The article expressly makes the rights independent of a proclamation.
wrong.3: Leaving resources undeveloped does not remove the coastal state's rights or allow anyone to exploit them.

questions.src: 국제사법재판소 · Statute of the International Court of Justice, Article 41: https://icj-web.leman.un-icc.cloud/statute
questions.q: What is the purpose of provisional measures at the International Court of Justice before a final decision?
choices: changing the terms of a treaty
questions.fact: Under Article 41 of the ICJ Statute, [[preserving the parties' rights]] is the purpose of provisional measures.
questions.explain: Provisional measures protect the parties' rights while the case remains undecided. Their indication does not itself settle who wins the case on its merits.
blankDistractors: changing the terms of a treaty

wrong.0: Interim protection of rights is different from a final decision on the merits.
wrong.3: Provisional measures do not automatically create the Court's authority to decide a dispute.

questions.src: NOAA · What is the difference between a nautical mile and a knot? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/nautical-mile-knot.html
questions.q: Exactly how many meters are in one international nautical mile?
questions.fact: One international nautical mile is defined as [[1852 m]] in length.
questions.explain: Nautical miles measure distances at sea. A nautical mile is not the same length as a land mile.

wrong.2: This is one tenth of the correct length.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 독도의 자연환경 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=67
questions.q: Which wind direction is typical of winter on Dokdo, according to the Dokdo information system?
questions.fact: [[Northwesterly winds]] are the prevailing winter winds on Dokdo.
questions.explain: Northwesterly winds prevail in winter. A prevailing direction does not describe every gust.

wrong.0: The source associates this direction with summer.
wrong.2: This confuses a summer wind direction with the winter pattern.

questions.src: 포항지방해양수산청 · 도동항로표지관리소 · https://pohang.mof.go.kr/ko/page.do?menuIdx=2832
questions.q: What other name is used for the lighthouse at Ulleungdo's Dodong Aids to Navigation Station?
questions.fact: [[Haengnam Lighthouse]] is another name for Dodong Lighthouse on Ulleungdo.
questions.explain: The Pohang maritime office also calls Dodong Lighthouse Haengnam Lighthouse. It should not be confused with other lighthouses on Ulleungdo.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 울릉도사적 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0066659
questions.q: Who left the 1694 survey account Ulleungdo Sajeok?
questions.fact: The 1694 survey account Ulleungdo Sajeok is attributed to [[Jang Han-sang]] as its author.
questions.explain: Jang's account describes the island's terrain and resources. The survey date differs from the dates of surviving later copies.

questions.src: 국사편찬위원회 · 동국여지승람 · https://contents.history.go.kr/mobile/tg/view.do?levelId=tg_003_0990
questions.q: In which year was the first edition of Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam, compiled by No Sa-sin and others, published?
questions.fact: Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam first appeared in [[1481]] as a geographic compilation.
questions.explain: Distinguish the first edition from the later expanded Sinjeung edition. Related geographic works can have different publication histories.

wrong.2: This is twenty years before the first edition.

questions.src: 산림청 국가생물종지식정보시스템 · 섬기린초 · https://www.nature.go.kr/kbi/plant/pilbk/selectPlantPilbkDtl.do?plantPilbkNo=39772
questions.q: Which endemic stonecrop-family plant of Ulleungdo and Dokdo bears yellow flowers in summer?
questions.fact: [[Seomgirincho]] is an endemic stonecrop-family plant of Ulleungdo and Dokdo with yellow flowers.
questions.explain: The national species database records its yellow flowers and distribution on the two islands. Use family and range as well as flower color.

wrong.0: This is an aster-family plant, not a stonecrop.

questions.src: NOAA · Why is the ocean salty? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/whysalty.html
questions.q: Which two ions make up the largest share of dissolved ions in seawater?
questions.fact: [[Sodium and chloride ions]] make up the largest combined share of seawater's dissolved ions.
questions.explain: Seawater contains a mixture of dissolved ions. Sodium and chloride account for most of that mixture.

wrong.0: Their role in shells does not make them the two dominant seawater ions.
wrong.1: These are not the main ions responsible for seawater's salinity.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part V · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part5.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 60, what is the usual maximum distance for an artificial island's safety zone, absent an international-standard exception?
questions.fact: Absent an international-standard exception, the safety zone normally extends at most [[500 m]] from the artificial island's outer edge.
questions.explain: Article 60(5) measures this distance from the outer edge. Internationally authorized exceptions and the actual zone width are separate matters.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part7.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS, where does a pursued ship's entry end a lawfully begun right of hot pursuit?
choices: the territorial sea of its flag state or a third state
the pursuing state's exclusive economic zone
the first stretch of high seas
questions.fact: The right of hot pursuit ends when the pursued ship enters [[the territorial sea of its flag state or a third state]] under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: the pursuing state's exclusive economic zone
questions.explain: Article 111(3) sets this stopping point. Simply reaching the high seas does not necessarily end a lawful pursuit.
blankDistractors: the pursuing state's exclusive economic zone
the first stretch of high seas

wrong.2: A lawful pursuit can continue onto the high seas when its conditions are met.
wrong.3: This is not the stopping point specified in the article.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part7.htm
questions.q: In UNCLOS, what does a ship's flag state mean?
choices: the state where the captain was born
the state granting the ship the right to fly its flag
the state that bought the cargo
the state with the nearest port
questions.fact: [[The state granting the ship the right to fly its flag]] is its flag state under UNCLOS.
questions.distractor: The state where the captain was born
questions.explain: Article 91 links a ship's nationality to its entitlement to fly a state's flag. The captain's birthplace or destination does not determine that nationality.
blankDistractors: the state where the captain was born
the state that bought the cargo
the state with the nearest port

wrong.0: A ship and its captain need not have the same nationality.
wrong.3: Distance to a port does not determine a ship's nationality.

questions.src: 포항지방해양수산청 · 독도항로표지관리소 · https://pohang.mof.go.kr/ko/page.do?menuIdx=2931 | 국회도서관 독도 · 독도 연표 1966~2000 · https://dokdo.nanet.go.kr/dokdo/front.dokdo?menu=chronology_8
questions.q: In which year did Dokdo Lighthouse become a staffed lighthouse?
questions.fact: Dokdo Lighthouse became a staffed lighthouse in [[1998]] with resident keepers.
questions.explain: Its first lighting and its conversion to staffed operation are different events. The maritime office dates the latter to December 1998.

questions.src: NOAA · What are phytoplankton? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/phyto.html
questions.q: Which green pigment helps phytoplankton use sunlight?
questions.fact: [[Chlorophyll]] is a key green pigment involved in phytoplankton photosynthesis.
questions.explain: Phytoplankton use light and nutrients to grow. Chlorophyll is a pigment central to their photosynthesis.

wrong.0: This oxygen-carrying protein is not the photosynthetic pigment asked for.
wrong.2: This is a structural protein, not a photosynthetic pigment.

questions.src: 국회도서관 독도 · 독도 연표 1966~2000 · https://dokdo.nanet.go.kr/dokdo/front.dokdo?menu=chronology_8
questions.q: In which year was Dokdo-ri established by an Ulleung County ordinance?
questions.fact: Dokdo-ri was established by county ordinance in [[2000]] as an administrative village.
questions.explain: The National Assembly Library dates the change to April 7, 2000. Creating an administrative unit is not the same as first acquiring sovereignty.

wrong.2: This is twenty years before Dokdo-ri was established.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 독도 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0015953
questions.q: Which two envoys from Ureungdo (Ulleungdo) presented local products to King Taejo of Goryeo in 930?
questions.fact: [[Baekgil and Todu]] were the envoys who brought local products from Ureungdo (Ulleungdo) to Goryeo in 930.
questions.explain: The record documents contact between the island and Goryeo. These envoys should not be confused with people active in later Joseon times.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 동람도 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0016361
questions.q: What printing method was used for the Dongnamdo maps in Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam?
questions.fact: [[Woodblock printing]] was used for the Dongnamdo maps included in Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam.
questions.explain: The maps were printed from carved blocks. Their production method matters alongside the place names they show.

wrong.1: The printing blocks here were wood, not copper.
wrong.3: The original maps were not produced photographically.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 육상생태계 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=68
questions.q: Which fern does the Dokdo Information System's land-ecology guide name for moist rock crevices?
questions.fact: The Dokdo land-ecology guide names [[Japanese holly fern]] in its account of moist rock crevices.
questions.explain: The Dokdo information system links this fern with damp crevices. It differs from the island's flowering coastal plants.

wrong.0: This flowering aster is not a fern.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 동람도 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0016361
questions.q: How many maps make up Dongnamdo in Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam?
questions.fact: Dongnamdo contains [[9 maps]] in total, counting its general and provincial maps.
questions.explain: There are eight provincial maps. The general map adds one more to the collection.

questions.src: International Court of Justice · The Court · https://www.icj-cij.org/court
questions.q: In which city is the International Court of Justice based?
questions.fact: [[The Hague]] is the city where the International Court of Justice is based.
questions.explain: The Court sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It is easy to confuse its location with other international institutions.

wrong.0: It is in the Netherlands, but the Court is in The Hague.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XVI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part16.htm
questions.q: What duty does UNCLOS Article 303 impose on states regarding archaeological and historical objects found at sea?
choices: a duty to grant unconditional ownership to the finder
a duty to auction them immediately
a duty to protect them and cooperate
a duty to assess only their present utility
questions.fact: [[A duty to protect them and cooperate]] applies to states under Article 303 for archaeological and historical objects found at sea.
questions.distractor: A duty to auction them immediately
questions.explain: The article emphasizes protection and cooperation. Finding an object does not automatically grant unrestricted disposal rights.
blankDistractors: a duty to grant unconditional ownership to the finder
a duty to auction them immediately
a duty to assess only their present utility

wrong.0: The article does not grant unconditional ownership to finders.
wrong.1: This replaces protection with an unsupported requirement to sell.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 해저퇴적물 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=96
questions.q: What is a particular advantage of collecting sediment cores around Dokdo?
choices: examining past environmental change through layers
questions.fact: [[Examining past environmental change through layers]] is a major purpose of sediment-core analysis.
questions.explain: Sediment layers can preserve records from different times. A core can reveal a history that a surface sample alone cannot show.

wrong.0: Wave periods are not obtained by reading sediment layers.
wrong.2: This confuses atmospheric measurements with seabed analysis.

questions.src: 우정사업본부 한국우표포털 · 독도의 자연, 2004년 갯메꽃 우표 · https://stamp.epost.go.kr/sp2/sg/spsg0102.jsp?page_num=1&tbsmh01seqnum=3945&tbsmh15seqnum=2422
questions.q: In which year was the first four-design Nature of Dokdo stamp set, including beach morning glory, issued?
questions.fact: The first Nature of Dokdo stamp set was issued in [[2004]] with four designs.
questions.explain: The postal service records January 16, 2004. This is the first set in that nature series, not the first-ever stamp depicting Dokdo.

questions.src: NOAA · What are spring and neap tides? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/springtide.html
questions.q: Around which lunar phases do spring tides, with a larger tidal range, generally occur?
questions.fact: Spring tides generally occur around [[new and full moon]] when tidal ranges are larger.
questions.explain: The Sun, Earth and Moon are nearly aligned at these phases. The word spring here does not restrict the tides to the spring season.

wrong.0: These phases are generally associated with neap tides.
wrong.2: First quarter does not belong in the correct pair.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VII · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part7.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS, can a land-locked state enjoy freedom of navigation on the high seas?
choices: a neighboring coastal state must permit every voyage
questions.fact: The principle that [[land-locked states also enjoy it]] applies to freedom of navigation on the high seas.
questions.explain: Article 87 recognizes high-seas freedoms for both coastal and land-locked states. A coastline is not required for this freedom.
blankDistractors: a neighboring coastal state must permit every voyage

wrong.0: The provision expressly includes land-locked states.
wrong.1: The rule does not depend on whether a state consists of islands.

questions.src: 국회도서관 독도 · 독도 연표, 조선 전기 · https://dokdo.nanet.go.kr/dokdo/front.dokdo?menu=chronology_3 | 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 독도 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0015953
questions.q: Who was sent to Ulleungdo as an inspector of Mureung and nearby places during King Taejong's reign?
questions.fact: [[Kim In-u]] served as the inspector sent to Ulleungdo during King Taejong's reign.
questions.explain: He appears in early-Joseon records of island inspection and relocation. He is distinct from earlier Goryeo investigators and later Joseon patrol officials.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 울릉도사적 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0066659
questions.q: In which county is the museum identified by the Korean encyclopedia as holding Ulleungdo Sajeok?
questions.fact: The Jomunguk Museum holding Ulleungdo Sajeok is located in [[Uiseong County]] in Korea.
questions.explain: The account is identified as a holding of Uiseong Jomunguk Museum. A document's subject and its repository need not be in the same place.

wrong.1: Its historical island links do not make it this repository's location.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 신증동국여지승람 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0033401
questions.q: How many volumes make up Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam?
questions.fact: Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam comprises [[55 volumes]] in its full arrangement.
questions.explain: The encyclopedia describes 55 volumes bound into 25 books. The textual divisions and the physical bound units are not the same count.

wrong.0: This confuses the 25 bound books with the volume count.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 해저퇴적물 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=96
questions.q: What does the occurrence of cold-water carbonate deposits around Dokdo show?
choices: carbonates accumulate only in the tropics
all carbonate sediment is volcanic ash
carbonate deposition can also occur in cold seas
cold seas have no biologically derived sediment
questions.fact: The statement that [[carbonate deposition can also occur in cold seas]] is supported by deposits around Dokdo.
questions.distractor: carbonates accumulate only in the tropics
questions.explain: Volcanic fragments and cold-water carbonates are both reported around Dokdo. Carbonate sediment alone does not prove a tropical setting.
blankDistractors: carbonates accumulate only in the tropics
all carbonate sediment is volcanic ash
cold seas have no biologically derived sediment

wrong.0: This contradicts the cold-water example at Dokdo.
wrong.1: They can occur together, but they are different materials.

questions.src: NOAA National Data Buoy Center · Wave calculations · https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/faq/wavecalc.shtml
questions.q: In the traditional definition of significant wave height, what fraction of the highest waves is averaged?
questions.fact: The traditional significant wave height averages the highest [[one third]] of the waves.
questions.explain: This is not the height of the single largest wave. Instruments can also estimate an equivalent significant height from the wave spectrum.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 중형저서동물 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=83
questions.q: In which year was the new species Prochaetosoma dokdoense reported?
questions.fact: The study describing Prochaetosoma dokdoense as a new species was published in [[2010]] in Marine Biology Research.
questions.explain: The Dokdo system identifies a March 2010 publication. A species-description date is not the date when the organism first evolved.

wrong.2: This is one year before the reported publication.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part XII · https://static.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part12.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 198, what should a state do upon learning of an imminent pollution threat to other states?
choices: notify only after cleanup is complete
immediate notice to affected states and competent organizations
privately notify only its own ships
questions.fact: Article 198 requires [[immediate notice to affected states and competent organizations]] when such a pollution threat becomes known.
questions.distractor: notice only after cleanup is complete
questions.explain: The duty concerns timely warning when the threat becomes known. Cleanup or compensation need not finish before notification.
blankDistractors: notify only after cleanup is complete
privately notify only its own ships

wrong.0: This improperly delays immediate notification.
wrong.2: This omits affected states and competent organizations.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 독도 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0015953
questions.q: Around which northern latitude is Dokdo located?
questions.fact: Dokdo lies at approximately [[37° N]] latitude.
questions.explain: Dokdo is near 37 degrees 14 minutes north. Latitude is distinct from longitude, which locates a place east or west.

wrong.0: This places Dokdo much too close to the equator.
wrong.3: Dokdo is in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.src: NOAA · Are corals animals or plants? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/coral.html
questions.q: What cannot be concluded solely because a coral has turned white through bleaching?
choices: that it has lost symbiotic algae
that its survival is under greater stress
questions.fact: Bleaching alone does not establish [[that it has already died]] when a coral turns white.
questions.explain: Bleaching involves stress and loss of symbiotic algae. A bleached coral can still be alive, though it faces a greater risk of death.
blankDistractors: that it has lost symbiotic algae
that its survival is under greater stress

wrong.1: This is part of the standard explanation of bleaching.
wrong.2: Bleaching does increase stress, so this is not the unsupported conclusion.

questions.src: NOAA SARSAT · 406 MHz Emergency Distress Beacons · https://www.sarsat.noaa.gov/emergency-406-beacons/
questions.q: Which frequency band does a maritime EPIRB use to alert Cospas-Sarsat satellites?
questions.fact: EPIRBs use the [[406 MHz]] band for Cospas-Sarsat satellite distress alerts.
questions.explain: The satellite alert band differs from signals used for local homing. NOAA identifies 406 MHz as the satellite distress band.

wrong.1: NOAA states that satellite detection at this frequency ended in 2009.

questions.src: 한국지도학회 · 최선웅, 개정일본여지노정전도의 지도학적 분석(2018), 초록 · https://www.dbpia.co.kr/journal/articleDetail?nodeId=NODE10769630
questions.q: Who completed the 1779 Kaisei Nihon Yochi Rotei Zenzu map?
questions.fact: [[Nagakubo Sekisui]] completed the Kaisei Nihon Yochi Rotei Zenzu map in 1779.
questions.explain: A study in the Korean cartographic journal identifies Nagakubo Sekisui as the maker. Other historical Japanese maps have different authors.

questions.src: 외교부 독도 · 독도 관련 주요 문서, 변영태 외무부장관 성명 · https://dokdo.mofa.go.kr/kor/pds/docu.jsp
questions.q: Which foreign minister described Dokdo as the first victim of Japan's aggression against the Korean Peninsula in October 1954?
questions.fact: [[Byun Yung-tai]] was the foreign minister who issued the relevant Dokdo statement on October 28, 1954.
questions.explain: The foreign ministry identifies its third minister, Byun Yung-tai, as the speaker. The statement should not be confused with later addresses.

questions.src: 우정사업본부 한국우표포털 · 독도의 자연, 2004년 갯메꽃 우표 · https://stamp.epost.go.kr/sp2/sg/spsg0102.jsp?page_num=1&tbsmh01seqnum=3945&tbsmh15seqnum=2422
questions.q: Which plant with pale-pink funnel-shaped flowers appears in the 2004 Nature of Dokdo stamp set?
questions.fact: [[Beach morning glory]] is the pale-pink funnel-flowered plant featured in the 2004 Nature of Dokdo stamps.
questions.explain: The stamp description identifies this coastal plant. The task is to match the pictured flower's description with its name.

wrong.1: This is not the pale-pink funnel-shaped flower described.

questions.src: NOAA · How Ghost Fishing Is Haunting Our Ocean · https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/about/media/how-ghost-fishing-haunting-our-ocean.html
questions.q: What is the continued capture of marine life by lost or abandoned nets and traps called?
questions.fact: [[Ghost fishing]] occurs when lost or abandoned fishing gear continues trapping marine life.
questions.explain: Nets and traps can keep catching animals without an operator. Recovering lost gear helps reduce that harm.

wrong.1: This involves farming organisms, not capture by lost gear.
wrong.3: This concerns seasonal movement of animals.

questions.src: NOAA · Frequency of Tides: The Lunar Day · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/tutorial_tides/tides05_lunarday.html
questions.q: About how long is a mean lunar day used in explaining tides?
questions.fact: A mean lunar day lasts about [[24 hours 50 minutes]] in the usual explanation of tides.
questions.explain: The Moon moves in its orbit, so Earth needs extra time to face it again. Actual tidal timing at a port also depends on local conditions.

wrong.0: This confuses the mean solar and lunar days.

questions.src: NOAA · What is Ocean Acidification? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/acidification.html | NOAA Ocean Acidification Program · What is Ocean Acidification? · https://oceanacidification.noaa.gov/what-is-ocean-acidification/
questions.q: As carbon dioxide absorption drives ocean acidification, what generally happens to pH?
questions.fact: The pH response to carbon-dioxide-driven ocean acidification is that [[it decreases]] over time.
questions.explain: Acidification means a shift toward lower pH. Seawater need not fall below pH 7 for this change to be called acidification.

wrong.0: This reverses the usual direction of acidification.
wrong.1: Acidification does not mean being fixed at a particular value.

questions.src: UN DOALOS · UNCLOS, Part VI · https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/part6.htm
questions.q: Under UNCLOS Article 79, whose consent is needed to delineate a pipeline route on the continental shelf?
questions.fact: Delineating a pipeline route on a coastal state's continental shelf requires consent from [[the coastal state]] under UNCLOS.
questions.explain: Article 79(3) addresses the route of pipelines. Its wording should not be treated as an identical rule for every submarine cable.

wrong.0: The manufacturing location does not determine this consent right.
wrong.1: This does not require unanimous approval by all UN members.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 성인봉 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0029504
questions.q: What is the highest peak on Ulleungdo?
questions.fact: [[Seonginbong]] is the highest peak on Ulleungdo.
questions.explain: Seonginbong stands in central Ulleungdo. It is distinct from the highest peaks of Dokdo's two main islets.

wrong.1: This mountain is on Jeju, not Ulleungdo.

questions.src: U.S. Geological Survey · Dissolved Oxygen and Water · https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/dissolved-oxygen-and-water
questions.q: What can aerobic microbial decomposition of organic matter do to dissolved oxygen?
choices: there is no connection with oxygen
questions.fact: During aerobic decomposition of organic matter, [[oxygen is consumed during decomposition]] in the water.
questions.distractor: there is no connection with oxygen
questions.explain: Active decomposition that uses oxygen can lower dissolved-oxygen levels. This does not treat anaerobic decomposition as the same process.
blankDistractors: there is no connection with oxygen

wrong.0: This reverses the possible oxygen demand from decomposition.
wrong.3: Oxygen consumption is not conversion into sea salt.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 독도 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0015953
questions.q: What is recorded as having been sent by Goryeo to Usan State after Jurchen raids in 1018?
questions.fact: [[Farming implements]] are recorded among the supplies Goryeo sent to Usan State in 1018.
questions.explain: The record concerns support for restoring livelihoods. It should be distinguished from accounts of military conquest.

wrong.0: These are not the livelihood supplies described in this record.
wrong.3: These do not match the period or recorded supplies.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 디지털장서각, 유하집 · https://jsg.aks.ac.kr/dir/view?catePath=%EC%88%98%EC%A7%91%EB%B6%84%EB%A5%98%2F%EC%99%95%EC%8B%A4&dataId=LIB_114123
questions.q: Whose poetry and prose are collected in the late-Joseon Yuhajip?
questions.fact: [[Hong Se-tae]] is the author whose work is collected in Yuhajip.
questions.explain: The Jangseogak catalog identifies Hong Se-tae as the author. Authorship differs from later editing and publication.

questions.src: 국회도서관 독도 · 삼국접양지도 · https://dokdo.nanet.go.kr/dokdo/collection/collectionDetail.dokdo?collection_sid=1
questions.q: Who produced Sangoku Tsuran Zusetsu and its attached Sangoku Setsujo no Zu map in 1785?
questions.fact: [[Hayashi Shihei]] produced Sangoku Tsuran Zusetsu and its attached regional map in 1785.
questions.explain: The National Assembly Library identifies Hayashi Shihei as the maker. The regional map also formed part of an illustrated book.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 어류 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=89 | 국립생태원 · 붉은박쥐 Myotis rufoniger · https://www.nie.re.kr/nie/pgm/edSpecies/view.do?menuNo=200127&speciesSn=4 | 국립해양생물자원관 MBRIS · 놀래기 Halichoeres tenuispinis · https://www.mbris.kr/pub/marine/tsearch/tsearchDetail.do?spcTxnId=270000007742 | 국립해양생물자원관 MBRIS · 황놀래기 Pseudolabrus sieboldi · https://www.mbris.kr/pub/marine/tsearch/tsearchDetail.do?spcTxnId=270000014823
questions.q: Which large wrasse seen at Dokdo develops a prominent forehead in mature males and crushes hard-shelled prey?
questions.fact: [[Asian sheepshead wrasse]] is the large wrasse at Dokdo whose mature males develop a prominent forehead.
questions.explain: The Dokdo system describes its forehead and strong teeth. The Korean name ends in dom, but it belongs among wrasses.

wrong.0: This is not the large wrasse described.

questions.src: UN Treaty Series · UNCLOS, authentic texts and conclusion date · https://www.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/unclos_f.pdf
questions.q: How many languages have equally authentic texts of UNCLOS?
questions.fact: UNCLOS has equally authentic texts in [[6 languages]] under its final provisions.
questions.explain: The six are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. A helpful translation is not necessarily an authentic treaty text.

wrong.0: This incorrectly restricts the texts to two languages.

questions.src: NOAA National Marine Sanctuaries · Seagrass Meadows · https://sanctuaries.noaa.gov/visit/ecosystems/seagrass.html
questions.q: Which botanical feature distinguishes seagrasses from seaweeds?
choices: being flowering plants that produce seeds
questions.fact: Seagrasses differ from seaweeds in [[being flowering plants that produce seeds]] underwater.
questions.explain: Seagrasses have true roots and leaves. Not every plant-like organism underwater is a seaweed.

wrong.0: Seagrasses do photosynthesize.
wrong.2: Seagrasses live submerged.

questions.src: U.S. Geological Survey · Dissolved Oxygen and Water · https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/dissolved-oxygen-and-water
questions.q: With salinity, pressure and other conditions equal, which water can hold more dissolved oxygen?
choices: it is always equal regardless of temperature
questions.fact: [[Colder water]] can hold more dissolved oxygen when other conditions are equal.
questions.explain: Temperature affects oxygen solubility. Actual ocean oxygen levels also depend on biological activity and mixing.
blankDistractors: it is always equal regardless of temperature

wrong.1: This reverses the temperature-solubility relationship.
wrong.2: Temperature does affect oxygen solubility.

questions.src: UN Treaty Series · UNCLOS, authentic texts and conclusion date · https://www.un.org/Depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/unclos_f.pdf
questions.q: In which year was UNCLOS concluded at Montego Bay?
questions.fact: UNCLOS was concluded in [[1982]] at Montego Bay.
questions.explain: It was concluded on December 10, 1982. Conclusion, global entry into force and entry into force for a particular state are different dates.

wrong.3: This is one year after conclusion.

questions.src: 국회도서관 독도 · 독도 연표 1966~2000 · https://dokdo.nanet.go.kr/dokdo/front.dokdo?menu=chronology_8
questions.q: Which year does the National Assembly Library's 1966–2000 chronology give for regular telephone service on Dongdo (East Islet)?
questions.fact: The National Assembly Library's 1966–2000 chronology places the Dongdo (East Islet) regular telephone opening in [[1997]], on March 24.
questions.explain: The National Assembly Library chronology records the opening on March 24, 1997. This is a telephone-service milestone, not the date of a lighthouse or mobile-phone facility.

questions.src: NOAA · What are plankton? · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/plankton.html
questions.q: What is the main basis for classifying marine organisms as plankton?
choices: a size visible only through a microscope
a lifetime attached to the seabed
limited ability to swim against currents
questions.fact: Plankton are characterized by [[limited ability to swim against currents]] while drifting in the water.
questions.distractor: a size visible only through a microscope
questions.explain: Plankton range from microscopic organisms to large jellyfish. Drifting with currents matters more than simply being small.
blankDistractors: a size visible only through a microscope
a lifetime attached to the seabed

wrong.0: Some plankton are large enough to see without a microscope.
wrong.1: Living attached to the bottom does not define plankton.

questions.src: 한국학중앙연구원 · 한국민족문화대백과사전, 대동지지 · https://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0014282
questions.q: Which final geographical work did Kim Jeong-ho compile to accompany his Daedongyeojido map?
questions.fact: Kim Jeong-ho compiled [[Daedongjiji]] as his final geographical work, intended to accompany Daedongyeojido.
questions.explain: Daedongjiji was designed for use alongside a map. A geographical text can supply details that are difficult to show on a map.

questions.src: 외교부 독도 · 대구시보 1947년 6월 20일 기사 역문 · https://dokdo.mofa.go.kr/m/kor/pds/part03_view09.jsp
questions.q: Which newspaper carried the June 20, 1947 Dokdo article reproduced in the foreign ministry's collection?
questions.fact: The June 20, 1947 Dokdo article reproduced by the foreign ministry appeared in [[Daegu Sibo]], a newspaper.
questions.explain: The ministry provides the original article and a modern Korean rendering. This question identifies the newspaper, rather than independently proving every event reported in it.

wrong.0: Do not confuse this publication with Dokdo reporting from 1906.

questions.src: 외교부 독도 · 관보 1900년 10월 27일, 칙령 제41호 역문 · https://dokdo.mofa.go.kr/kor/pds/part02_view03.jsp
questions.q: What county rank did Article 1 of Imperial Edict No. 41 assign to Uldo County?
questions.fact: Article 1 of Imperial Edict No. 41 assigned Uldo County [[rank 5]] within the county classification.
questions.explain: The edict sets rank 5 and refers to expenses for that rank in Article 4. This was an administrative classification, not a school grade.

wrong.3: This does not match the rank written in the edict.

questions.src: 경북대학교 울릉도·독도연구소 · 초종용 · https://dokdoknu.com/wp/?p=2727 | KISTI ScienceON · 울릉도, 독도 초종용에서 형태 변이와 지리적 분포 양상 · https://scienceon.kisti.re.kr/srch/selectPORSrchArticle.do?cn=JAKO201609633506561
questions.q: Which herb recorded on Dokdo is parasitic on other plants?
questions.fact: [[Chojongyong (broomrape)]] is a parasitic herb recorded on Dokdo.
questions.explain: Kyungpook National University's institute describes Chojongyong as a parasitic plant of Ulleungdo and Dokdo. A parasite and the plants growing beside it are not the same.

wrong.0: The parasitic plant identified in this source is Chojongyong.

questions.src: 해양수산부·한국해양과학기술원 독도종합정보시스템 · 중형저서동물 · https://www.dokdo.re.kr/home/cms/cmsCont.do?cntnts_sn=83
